label: Impossible Objects of Desire
release_notes: David Best - vocals, guitar; Steve Lewis - keyboards, backing vocals; Ben Adamo - bass, backing vocals; Ed Chivers - drums, backing vocals (Under the Radar).

Producer, studio and mastering are not published. Made over four years of sessions on England's south coast; the plan to record it live was scaled back to a direct, melody-first approach (press release). Clash says one of the songs is an instrumental but does not say which.

Lineage: Best and Lewis started the band in Brighton in 1999. Matt Hainsby played bass on the breakthrough Transparent Things era; Adamo and Chivers joined by 2016. Albums include Transparent Things, Lightbulbs, Ventriloquizzing, Artificial Sweeteners and Slight Variations (Wikipedia, AllMusic). On their own Impossible Objects of Desire label after leaving Yep Roc.

Krautrock lineage (Neu!, CAN, Kraftwerk) with Talking Heads and New Order in the pop (Clash). Themes are loss, fatherhood and ageing; 158 is about the death of Best's friend and former band member Matthew Collins, aka Grunder (That Eric Alper).

pull_quotes.text: a slinky return that thrives on immediacy
pop hewn from the DNA of Talking Heads and New Order

draft_comment: Brighton krautpop lifers still locking into a groove, with Neu! in the bedrock and Talking Heads and New Order up top, per Clash. Out Oct. 30, and only the first single has posted lyrics, so the FCC screen is mostly open.

tracks.title: Lowest Common Denominator
tracks.notes: Slinky, sloping bassline in the vein of Bush Tetras (Stereogum, press release). Dance-minded, built to make people dance (Best). Wonky post-punk pop

tracks.title: Point 33 Recurring
tracks.notes: Taut, built around repetition (press coverage). Shortest track on the record

tracks.title: No Green Light
tracks.notes: Long track. Infinite motorik groove, the closest to the band's trademark sound on the record (mxdwn). Band says more A23 than autobahn. Written to anticipate the energy of their live shows (press coverage)
